$comment: The CLOSED set of installable modules this repository may publish, and the
facts each release is checked against. A package absent from this file
cannot be built or published by `release-module.yml` — the workflow resolves
its target here and fails closed, so adding a publishable module is a
reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time string.
`dotmac-kernel` and `dotmac-ui` are deliberately NOT here: they have their
own workflows with their own inspection rules (a kernel wheel must ship
compiled CSS; a module must not). One workflow pretending to cover both
would have to weaken whichever check the other cannot satisfy.
kernel_floor is the EARLIEST kernel that can actually load and register
the module — the highest of everything the module needs, not one fixed
rule. Two things set it:
1. the release that allocated its schema in MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER; an
earlier kernel raises UnallocatedNamespaceError and the module cannot
register at all;
2. the release that added any kernel CAPABILITY the manifest consumes —
e.g. ADR-0023's `platform_tables`; an earlier kernel raises TypeError
at import, before the allocation check is reached.
A capability floor names the earliest INSTALLABLE kernel carrying it, not
the source release that introduced it. A floor naming an unpublished
version cannot be resolved by an installer, so it is not a floor at all.
Worked example, spelled out because it is easy to over-apply:
`ModuleManifest.platform_tables` entered kernel SOURCE at a53, but a53-a55
were never published, so a56 is the first installable kernel carrying it.
a56 is therefore the floor of a module whose HIGHEST consumed capability
is `platform_tables` — dotmac-release-catalog and
dotmac-entitlement-allocation, which are platform-only and stop there.
It is NOT the floor of every dual-plane module. One consuming a LATER
capability floors at that one instead: dotmac-ticketing consumes ADR-0028
plane selection and floors at a61. Take the highest capability the module
actually consumes, then round UP to the first published release carrying
it. Historical changelog entries may still say a53 — that is where the
source landed, not where a consumer can get it.
For most modules (1) is the answer and (2) does not apply. Where both
apply the higher wins, and tests/architecture/test_kernel_version_sync.py
keeps the two cases in separate, reasoned maps so neither is silent.
Either way registry verification can only pass once that kernel is
published.
## dotmac-imports was REMOVED from this file on 2026-08-15
It sat here, allowlisted, with no `dotmac-imports-v` tag in any version.
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py` surfaced that as an anomaly, and
the anomaly turned out to be THIS ROW rather than the missing tag: the
package's own EXTRACTION.toml `next_action` says to 'keep the module
audit-complete and unreleased until a real first adopter is ready' and to
'publish the exact kernel/imports releases just in time for that cutover'.
An allowlist row said the opposite, and an allowlist row is how this
repository states that a package may be published.
So the row is gone and the PACKAGE is untouched: it keeps its declared
0.1.0a2, its catalogue entry, its kernel floor and its dossier. Removal is
not retirement — it is the absence that is the safety mechanism, the rule
ADR-0026 section 8 set for dotmac-approvals and PR #180 applied to
dotmac-auth-oidc: the entry lands WITH the proof, never ahead of it.
The row is re-added with ERP's adoption proof, which the dossier names as
cutover 1 and gates behind the E8 Organization-to-Tenant and
composed-lineage decision. Until then the state is recorded, deliberately
and with its reason, in docs/inventories/declared-publication-baseline.json
so the next reader does not 'repair' it by dispatching a release.
kernel_floor is a68, a CAPABILITY raise above its a45 ledger
allocation and above the a56 `platform_tables` raise that preceded
it. a66 published `idempotency_ledger.v1`, the name for the
at-most-once tables `stage_allocation` writes at request time. Every
kernel from a18 HAS those tables, but one below a66 does not know the
NAME, so `ModuleManifest.__post_init__` -> `validate_prerequisites`
raises `UnknownPrerequisiteError` at manifest import, before the
allocation check is ever reached. a68 then published
`platform_audit_log.v1`, the second effect staging writes inside the
same operation. ea_0002 and ea_0003 verify those effects in provider
lineage order; both are DDL-free and both are required wheel content.
EVERY migration is a required wheel content, deliberately. This
repository does not compose the module — `app/assembly.py` omits it,
`alembic.ini` carries no `ea` lineage, and an import-linter contract
forbids the assembly importing it, because allocating is the vendor
half and a data plane installing it would acquire the wrong one
(ruling C4). A wheel that shipped the manifest but dropped a migration
would therefore fail first in the vendor control plane's deployment,
not here. ea_0002 and ea_0003 are the load-bearing ones for this rule:
they create nothing, so a wheel that dropped either would install a
module whose prerequisite is declared and never verified — exactly
the state a6 exists to end.
Listed for the ERP-first ticket adoption programme (ADR-0017's
2026-08-13 ticketing amendment). Until this entry existed the module
was unpublishable, so no product could pin it and the dossier's

kernel_floor is a61, NOT the a39 that allocated mod_tkt. A CAPABILITY
has raised this floor three times, and the field must always name the
LAST of them:
- `platform_tables` (dual-plane, ADR-0023) — source a53, first

- the logical prerequisite contract (ADR-0006 D1 amendment) its
manifest and migration root use — a56;
- ADR-0028 plane selection: the manifest declares
`supported_plane_sets` and tk_0001 calls `selected_module_planes` —
An earlier kernel cannot import the manifest, so the check never
reaches the allocation. The floor is set by a kernel capability rather
than by this module's own namespace row.
This prose said a56 while the field said a61 — the exact field/comment
drift the a49 correction existed to remove. a56 is the stopping point
for the PLATFORM-ONLY modules, which consume nothing after
`platform_tables`; ticketing consumes plane selection and goes further.
`alembic` is in allowed_requires and is NOT a packaging slip:
`dotmac_ticketing.linking`'s per-plane link helpers emit DDL into a
CONSUMING product's migration, so Alembic is imported at runtime by
them rather than used as a dev tool. The other modules ship no such
helper and correctly forbid it.
mod_files is allocated in a54; a56 is the first published kernel with
the prerequisite contract consumed by fi_0001. a3 raises the operative

`jsonschema` IS a runtime dependency from a6: capability declarations
publish Draft 2020-12 schemas and the lifecycle validates them before
configuration can be written, bound or enabled. Listing it is not a
general dependency escape; the PR-time exact-set gate keeps every
module's declared dependencies equal to this reviewed closure.
`secret_refs.py` is a required wheel content because it is the ADR-0024 § 7
enforcement point — a wheel that shipped the models but dropped the refusal
would accept secret VALUES into an immutable config revision and never
complain. It was named `secrets.py` until the release wheel-content policy
correctly refused it; renamed rather than exempted.
`runtime_policy.py` is the SPI 1.3 projection point. If a wheel dropped
it, a connector could declare boundaries while the sole runtime had no
provider-neutral way to derive the exact egress union or refuse an old
manifest whose boundary is still omitted.

The ADR-0033 vendor module cohort. All four are listed together because
they are released together: the modules floor on kernel 0.1.0a77 and
0.1.0a77 exists to carry their four MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER rows, so a
kernel release with no module beside it satisfies nothing and a module
release without it cannot resolve.
kernel_floor is 0.1.0a77 for all four, and for three of them that is NOT
their own allocation release. The cohort was built as four stacked pull
requests, each bumping the kernel to carry its own row - a74 (`cg`), a75
(`li`), a76 (`dc`), a77 (`bp`) - and a kernel release publishes ONE
version, so a74..a76 exist as changelog history rather than as artifacts.
a77 is the first INSTALLABLE kernel carrying any of the four allocations,
which is what makes it the floor of all four. Same rule the a53..a55 gap
already forced on `platform_tables`, applied to an allocation instead of
to a capability; the reasoning is in
tests/architecture/test_kernel_version_sync.py's
UNPUBLISHED_ALLOCATION_FLOORS, and a tag-reading test refuses a floor
that skips a kernel which would have run the module.
EVERY source module and EVERY migration is required wheel content. This
repository composes none of the four - `app/assembly.py` omits them and
`alembic.ini` carries no `cg`, `li`, `dc` or `bp` lineage, because the
starter is a target application and these are the vendor control plane's
capabilities - so a wheel that shipped the manifest and dropped a module
would fail first in an ADOPTER's deployment rather than here. That is the
same argument dotmac-integration, dotmac-approvals and
dotmac-application-directory record, and it is why the required list is
the whole package rather than a sample of it.
Listing them is what unblocks the composition. `dotmac_vendor_control_plane`
cannot pin an unpublished module, so every `first_cutover` in this cohort
was unreachable by construction while these rows were absent - and
publication remains gated separately by
docs/inventories/declared-publication-baseline.json, which still carries a
row for each of the four. An allowlist row makes a module PUBLISHABLE; it
does not assert that it has been published or adopted.

`allowed_requires` carries no crypto library, and that is a boundary
rather than an omission: this module holds no private key column and
implements no signer. `LicenceSigner` is a port the ADOPTING assembly
fills over its own secret seam (ADR-0009 - a secret is held, never
dereferenced), so a crypto dependency appearing here would mean the
boundary had moved and the exact-set gate should refuse the release.

`dc_0001` is required wheel content for a reason stronger than the

exactly the gap tests/test_deployment_control_platform_isolation.py
proves closed against a real database.

`dotmac-ui` in `allowed_requires` is the first time a module in this
lane declares a first-party dependency other than the kernel, and it
is the approved presentation boundary rather than an escape: dotmac-ui
owns the token vocabulary, the projection and contrast validation,
this module owns the scoped VALUES, and the assembly maps one into the
other. The dependency direction is the published one
(assembly -> module -> dotmac-ui -> dotmac-kernel), and dotmac-ui
0.1.0a7 is released, so the floor resolves. Vendoring a hex parser or
a contrast check to avoid the dependency would create the second
owner ADR-0006 U1 exists to prevent.
`brand_values.py` is required wheel content because it is where the
allowlist lives: BRAND_OVERRIDE_INPUTS names the only two values that
may cross into `dotmac_ui.BrandOverride`, and every other legacy
semantic colour is dispositioned in code rather than in prose. A wheel
that shipped the models and dropped it would install a module whose
stated boundary is enforced nowhere.
